title: An analysis of iterative refinement for quantum linear system solvers
authors: Adrian Harkness, Mohammadhossein Mohammadisiahroudi, Brandon Augustino, Giacomo Nannicini, Tamás Terlaky
abstract: We present and analyze an iterative refinement (IR) framework for improving the precision dependence of algorithms that combine a quantum linear system algorithm (QLSA) with quantum state tomography. Existing QLSAs achieve polylogarithmic dependence on the inverse error tolerance to prepare a quantum state encoding the solution, but extracting a classical description of such a state via tomography typically introduces a polynomial dependence on the target precision. To retain polylogarithmic dependence in the inverse error tolerance throughout the entire process, we develop an IR scheme that solves a sequence of related linear systems to progressively refine the solution while requiring only fixed-precision quantum subroutines, finally obtaining a classical description of a high-precision solution. We analyze the proposed framework under three input models: quantum-read/classical-write RAM (QRAM), linear combinations of unitaries (LCU), and sparse-access oracles. We evaluate the proposed scheme through numerical experiments on both quantum simulators and real quantum hardware. The results demonstrate that iterative refinement efficiently improves the precision of the solution and exhibits robustness to hardware noise.
summary: This paper introduces an Iterative Refinement (IR) framework to solve quantum linear systems, overcoming a major limitation where standard methods suffer from polynomial resource scaling with required precision. By using repeated, fixed-precision quantum circuits, the IR scheme maintains polylogarithmic resource scaling, making high-accuracy quantum computation more feasible. The analysis validates this approach across various quantum hardware models.
main_problem: The primary challenge is mitigating the polynomial dependence on target precision ($\epsilon^{-1}$) that arises when combining quantum linear system algorithms (QLSA) with quantum state tomography (QTA).
main_result: The authors propose an Iterative Refinement (IR) framework that retains polylogarithmic dependence on the inverse error tolerance throughout the entire process.
method: The IR scheme solves a sequence of related linear systems using only fixed-precision quantum subroutines, progressively refining the solution to achieve high accuracy.
model_or_system: The analysis is conducted within the framework of quantum computation, specifically addressing the Quantum Linear System Problem (QLSP) for solving $A\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{b}$. The framework is tested across three input models: QRAM, LCU, and sparse-access oracles.
key_observables: Residual error ($\|x - A^{-1}b\| \le \epsilon$), cumulative circuit depth, and resource scaling (QRAM accesses, oracle queries).
important_parameters: Condition number ($\kappa_A$), sparsity ($s$), and target precision ($\epsilon$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the success of quantum algorithms with probability $\ge 1 - \delta$ and relies on the ability to perform fixed-precision quantum subroutines repeatedly.
figures_summary: Figures compare the cumulative circuit depth of direct HHL versus HHL+IR, showing IR maintains a constant per-iteration cost while achieving higher precision, avoiding the staircase depth scaling of direct methods.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the limitation of current QLSAs regarding precision scaling, then introduces and analyzes the IR framework across multiple input models, followed by numerical validation on simulators and hardware.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the practical bottleneck of achieving high-precision results in quantum simulation and computation by providing a resource-efficient algorithmic structure.
